data.narrative:
Nordic Air Defence, a seed-stage defense and security company founded by Karl Rosander, was analyzed against a comparable universe of 10 private and 2 public peers operating in the Defense & Security sector. The private peer set includes UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic; public comparables trade under DRSHF and IDEAFORGE.NS.

Peer-median valuation methodology was applied using four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Stark Defence (Series A, $4.0B), UFORCE (Seed, $1.0B), Singularity (Series A, $400M), and NODA AI (Series A, $125M). The median valuation across this set is $700M, with a range spanning $125M to $4.0B. This method's wide dispersion reflects stage and focus-area heterogeneity within the defense tech segment—seed-stage companies command substantially different multiples depending on underlying capability maturity and customer traction.

The triangulated valuation range is $595M to $805M, centered on $700M. This analysis relies on a single method given available data constraints, creating meaningful uncertainty around the point estimate. Key variables affecting valuation include: stage-appropriate revenue or customer metrics (not provided), technology differentiation relative to the peer set, and defense sector funding momentum. The wide peer range ($125M–$4.0B) underscores sensitivity to deal-specific factors and suggests the median should be treated as directional rather than definitive absent additional quantitative anchors.
